claims.evidence: The witness report describes the console as blue.
The witness identified the brand but could not confirm the specific model (null).
No physical game discs or digital library screenshots were included in the report.
PES 2027 is not a real product; the PES series was rebranded to eFootball years ago and no 2027 version exists.

risks.risk: Console may be a lower-value model (Fat) or have a hardware defect (BLOD).
risks.proof: A video of the console booting to the home screen and a photo of the model sticker.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a non-functional PS4 Fat model.

risks.risk: The '10 games' may be digital accounts that the buyer cannot keep or modded files on a jailbroken system.
risks.proof: Photos of physical game discs or a video of games launching while signed out of PSN.

risks.risk: The internal storage may be the minimum 500GB or a failing hard drive.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'System Storage' menu in settings.

risks.risk: The plastic wrap may be hiding significant scratches or cracks on the console surface.
risks.proof: Photos of the console with the plastic film removed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as 'Fair' condition with cosmetic damage.

proof_requests: Photo of the model and serial number sticker on the back/bottom of the console.
Video of the console powering on and navigating the menu.
Screenshot of the 'Storage' section in System Settings.
Photos of any physical game discs included.
Photo of the console without the plastic wrap.
response.reason: The witness confirms the item is a PlayStation console, allowing for a worst-case valuation of a base PS4 model, though the seller's claim of 'PES 2027' is impossible and suggests the games have no market value.
